question: What is the internet primarily defined as?

options.B: A global network of connected computers
options.D: A collection of web pages only

explanation: The internet is a vast physical and digital infrastructure linking computers worldwide, whereas the web is just one way information is shared across it. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does the World Wide Web work alongside the internet?

options.A: The web is a service running on the internet infrastructure
options.B: The web handles hardware while the internet handles software
options.C: The internet is created by individual web browser windows
options.D: The web and the internet are completely separate systems

explanation: Think of the internet as the actual highway, and the web as the vehicles carrying information back and forth on it! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: When data travels across a computer network, what are the small pieces called?
explanation: Correct! Large files are broken down into tiny pieces called 'packets' so they can zip across the network quickly and piece back together at the end. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why are local servers and offline data storage so important in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: To replace the need for trained nursing documentation
options.B: To prevent patients from seeing their own medical records
options.C: To stop computers from using electrical power
options.D: To maintain care when internet connectivity fluctuates

explanation: Spot on! Because network signals can be unpredictable, having local backups ensures you can always pull up vital patient files without breaking a sweat. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which free online search engine is best for finding biomedical and health science research?
explanation: You nailed it. PubMed is a nurse's best friend for searching millions of reliable research articles and abstracts for studies. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: You want to find reliable, high-quality systematic reviews to update a ward wound care routine. Where should you look first?
explanation: Great choice! The Cochrane Library is famous for gold-standard, rigorous systematic reviews that give you rock-solid evidence for your practice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main focus of telemedicine?

options.A: Manual pill counting in hospital pharmacies
options.B: Physical paper record archiving in basements
options.D: Remote diagnosis and treatment using technology

explanation: That's right! Telemedicine bridges the distance between patients and clinicians using phone or video calls when they aren't in the same room. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h4)

question: How does m-health (mobile health) particularly help healthcare delivery in rural or resource-limited areas?

options.A: By utilizing mobile phones for community health tracking
options.B: By stopping the spread of all infectious diseases instantly
options.C: By ensuring all patients have free smartphones provided
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for any physical hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Since almost everyone has a mobile phone, nurses and health workers can easily follow up on patients right in their communities. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h4)

question: What kind of security technology scrambles web data to keep it safe while it travels online?
explanation: Correct! SSL encryption locks up your data like a secure parcel so prying eyes can't read it while it's moving across the network. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why is it a big safety risk to share patient photos on everyday social media apps?

options.A: It slows down the internet speed for other wards
options.B: It uses up too much electricity on the ward
options.C: It automatically deletes all hospital records
options.D: It violates patient privacy and data security

explanation: Exactly. Patient confidentiality is sacred—posting identifiable info online breaks trust and violates professional code. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is one of the biggest dangers of health information found casually on the internet?

options.A: Mandatory use in all teaching hospitals

explanation: You got it! Anyone can post anything online, so we always have to double-check sources to avoid spreading harmful health advice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h6)

question: When checking out a health website, why is it smart to look out for who is sponsoring or funding it?

options.A: Sponsors pay for the internet service in the hospital
options.B: Financial backers may bias the information presented
options.C: Commercial sites never contain any scientific facts
options.D: Sponsored sites are always completely illegal to read

explanation: Spot on. Companies funding a site might push products or views that benefit their pockets rather than pure clinical truth. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which of these actions is a clear example of unprofessional internet use by a nurse?

options.A: Searching PubMed for evidence-based wound care
options.B: Participating in an accredited online nursing webinar
options.C: Reading hospital policy documents on an intranet
options.D: Posting identifiable patient details on social media

explanation: Correct! Patient details belong in secure records, never on public social media timelines. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why do nursing regulatory bodies strictly enforce rules about digital professionalism?

options.A: To stop nurses from owning personal smartphones
options.B: To maintain public trust and protect patient confidentiality
options.C: To prevent nurses from reading medical journals
options.D: To make hospital computer systems run faster

explanation: You nailed it! Protecting patient privacy online is just as important as protecting it at the bedside to keep the public's trust. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h7)
